newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices up yr/yr 2.8 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices up yr/yr 2.8 pct in Jan.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following retail price indices for January:
RETAIL PRICES INDEX JAN DEC JAN 96
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax -0.1 -0.1 -0.2
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI down 0.2 pct MM, +2.7 pct YY, RPIX +3.0 pct YY, RPIY +2.6 pct YY.
The ONS said the monthly fall in household goods prices was the biggest fall since records began in 1956. The same applied to the fall in clothing and footwear prices.
The rise in the headline RPI year-on-year rate was largely attributable to housing costs, where a significant rise in mortgage rates contrasted with a fall this time last year.

There were smaller upward effects from food prices, particularly those for seasonal food and from motoring costs. Downward pressures on the 12-month rate came from prices for fuel and light, household goods and clothing and footwear.
The bulk of the rise in food prices was due to fresh vegetable prices rising considerably as bad weather affected supplies. There was also a small upward effect from eggs.
Looking forward to February, the ONS said the RPI index will be calculated using a revised basket of goods.
Seasonal food prices generally rise in February. The weather will continue to affect fresh vegetables.
Coffee prices are likely to rise following the recent dramatic rise in world coffee prices.
The recent five percent revaluation of the green pound may lead to some reductions for butter and sugar.
A small rise in mortgage payments is expected as October's interest rate rise continues to feed through. The annual effect will be compounded by falling mortgage rates in February last year.
Telephone charges are expected to fall while fares and travel prices will increase following annual price revisions. These come through a month later than last year.
